migration.owner: Twenty entrypoint bootstrap followed by fail-closed instance and workspace command runners
migration.command: Twenty target entrypoint, then yarn command:prod run-instance-commands, then yarn command:prod upgrade; the 2.54 upgrade sequence contains every instance and workspace command from 1.21 on, so 2.24 upgrades in one step

rollback.boundary: Vor dem ersten Start des Zielservers darf das Quellimage erneut gestartet werden. Nach einer Zielmigration wird kein älteres Image gegen die vorwärts migrierte Datenbank gestartet.

migration.command: rustfs /data on the existing volume. 1.0.4 reads the beta.11 object, bucket and IAM format in place and only adds pool identity, bucket incarnation and scanner state files under .rustfs.sys. The IAM migration in the 1.0 notes converts MinIO .minio.sys data and is skipped on a RustFS volume. Image user (uid 10001), entrypoint, data path and environment variables are unchanged.

rollback.boundary: Before the target writes, the source image may start again. After 1.0.4 has run on the volume, LeonAid does not rely on a binary rollback: the full RustFS volume is restored from the recovery point, together with Core PostgreSQL.

migration.command: infra/upgrade/twenty-queue-store.sh migrate: stop twenty-server, drain BullMQ queues with the old twenty-worker, empty the Redis 7.4 volume (RDB 12 is unreadable for Valkey)

rollback.boundary: Valkey writes RDB format VALKEY080, which Redis 7.4 cannot read. An older release therefore never starts on the migrated volume; rollback restores Twenty into a new project, where the queue store starts empty and twenty-server registers its cron jobs again.

migration.owner: PostgreSQL minor release within major version 16
migration.command: Recreate core-postgres and twenty-postgres with the target image on the existing data volumes; a minor release keeps the on-disk format, so neither dump/restore nor pg_upgrade runs

rollback.boundary: PostgreSQL 16.9 can start on a data directory written by 16.15 of the same major version. LeonAid still restores both databases from the recovery point, because Core and Twenty migrations run in the same release window.
Nach einer vorwärts laufenden Core-Migration wird kein Code-Rollback gegen das neue Schema behauptet.
